requests.what: register the control-loader reason `defect-or-expect-empty` (a control whose defect or expect is empty, or whose expect states no observable; repair: state the planted defect and the observable value, refusal code or failed row); BD-025's loader rule 4 now uses it.

testkit's `Control` type (Controls::for_gate) lists only id, seed, gate, kind, target, defect, expect; as the one parser of controls.toml it must also carry BD-025's optional fields feature, fixture, due, permanent, removed_check, last_seen and state (runnable | obligation, written by N38b-05's seeding), or BD-025's validator, which runs on the parser's rows, cannot check rules 3 and 5 or the obligation rule.

admit two optional fields on a [[ka]] row with label FACT, `rerun` (Boolean, false until the pilot or source has been reproduced here) and `rerun_receipt` (the receipt hash), the same pair N38b-05 uses on catalogue entries, and compute the eligibility `obligation: rerun` for a FACT row with rerun = false (reject rerun = true with no receipt). N09-KA's four pilot rows (KA-033 to KA-036) use them; today rule text only notes 'to be re-run before a gate cites it' and nothing computes it.

state how each seeded control's BD-025 fields are filled from the catalogue entry: target (the component the plant mutates), defect (from `shortcut`), expect (the observable refutation from `case`), and feature (the plant's Cargo feature, for a mutation) or fixture (for planted-input/design/world, from `plant`); BD-025's loader rejects an empty defect or expect (defect-or-expect-empty) and checks feature/fixture existence for gates not 'not-run', so seeding as now specified would write controls the loader rejects. N10-CX names plants '<planting bead>:cx-<nnn>' (or the named mutants such as 'N13-18:M2'), from which the feature is cx-<nnn>.
